ae54703ad48c.title: Automation
ae54703ad48c.content: What the automations do, and what they never do (section 11). Generated from requirements v0.5 by scripts/gen-requirements.ts; do not edit by hand. Cite one as req:aai-automation#<ID>. | ID | Level | Requirement | . | AUTO-01 | SHALL | Auto-add to the programme project: aai-programme issues of type Epic, Milestone, Research question, Dependency, Decision or Assumption, and workstream issues (including WS5 items in aai-programme) labelled thin-slice, sprint-demo, blocked or at-risk. Other WS5 items stay off the board and still roll up into their epics through sub-issues. The pilot confirms that the auto-add filter can select by issue type; if it cannot, use a GitHub Action and record this. GitHub limits the number of auto-add workflows per project depending on the plan. If the limit is reached, use a GitHub Action instead and record this. | . | AUTO-03 | SHALL | A GitHub Action, using the BD-08 credentials. When a programme epic, milestone, research question, dependency or decision issue is created, set Programme status to Not started unless a value was supplied. When a programme-tracked issue is closed as completed, set Done. When it is closed as not planned, set Cancelled. When it is reopened, set In progress. Built-in project workflows can only set a project’s own Status field, so they cannot do this. | . | AUTO-04 | SHALL | Delivery health roll-up. A scheduled Action finds blocked or at-risk labels on sub-issues and sets Delivery health on the parent epic to the worst signal found, in the order Blocked, then At risk, then On track. It never lowers or clears Delivery health; the epic’s owner does that. The PM has approved this rule. | . | AUTO-05 | SHALL NOT | No automation sets Integration readiness, Review status, Risk category, Impact, a decision or risk acceptance. | . | AUTO-06 | SHALL | Where a saved view or chart can do the job, use it instead of an Action. | . | AUTO-07 | SHALL | Document every automation in the programme project README: what triggers it, what it does, its scope and who owns it. | . | AUTO-08 | SHALL | All scripts are safe to rerun without creating duplicates and have a --dry-run mode. They live in aai-programme/scripts. | . | AUTO-09 | SHALL | If an automation needs a token or raised permissions, stop before creating the secret and report exactly what permission is needed. The BD-08 credentials are expected; any others are not. | . | AUTO-10 | SHALL | Validation check. The Technical Integration Lead confirms validation by adding a comment to the item that starts with Validation confirmed: followed by a short note or evidence link. A scheduled Action checks every item whose Integration readiness is Validated. If there is no confirmation comment from the Technical Integration Lead, it adds the validation-exception label and one comment explaining why. It is idempotent: it never adds a second comment for the same exception. When the confirmation comment appears, or the value moves off Validated, it removes the label. It never changes Integration readiness. The Technical Integration Lead’s GitHub username is a setting in aai-programme/scripts, not hard-coded. | . | AUTO-11 | SHALL | Backfill. Auto-add workflows only catch items created or updated after they are switched on. A one-off script, run in build step 8, adds existing qualifying items to the programme project. | . | AUTO-12 | MAY | Optional. A weekly script calculates M6 (average age of blocked items) from the issue timelines and posts it as a comment on a pinned “Programme metrics” issue in aai-programme. Not part of the pilot. Build it only after the pilot passes, and only if there is capacity; M1 to M5 are enough to start with. | .

8af572ce1955.title: Decisions needed before the build
8af572ce1955.content: What must be decided, and by whom, before the build goes past pre-flight (section 3). Each statement is the decision and its recommended default. Default: Decided: the existing World Health Organization organisation, shared with other WHO teams. Login: WorldHealthOrganization (https://github.com/WorldHealthOrganization) | . | BD-01a | SHALL | Shared organisation safeguards: (1) the current base permission for members. If it is anything other than “No permission”, partners invited as members could read other WHO teams’ repositories, and the build must not change it (SEC-05); (2) how many of the 25 organisation issue fields are already used by other teams; (3) which issue types already exist; (4) whether the owners will allow project-specific issue types, and pinning fields to them; (5) that the agent works through a named account with delegated rights, never a shared login. Default: WHO GitHub owner to confirm before step 2. If (1) cannot be met, partners join as outside collaborators instead (see BD-03) | . | BD-02 | SHALL | All Assured AI coordination repositories (programme and workstream repositories holding issues, features, stories and spikes) sit in that organisation. Default: Decided: yes | . | BD-02a | SHALL | Partner source-code repositories, models and other technical assets may stay in partners’ own GitHub organisations. Default: Decided: yes, where partners need it | . | BD-02b | SHALL | How each workstream will link external technical assets, if any, to its WHO-hosted coordination issues. Default: Workstream lead to confirm before bulk import | . | BD-03 | SHALL | Partners join as organisation members. Default: Decided: members, subject to BD-01a(1) and the checks in BD-03a. If the base permission cannot be “No permission”, fall back to outside collaborators with access granted per repository. Whichever model is used for partners and for Gates Foundation contacts is recorded in the build report and the programme README | . | BD-03a | SHALL | Checks before partners are invited: (1) whether the organisation uses SAML single sign-on or Enterprise Managed Users, and if so how partners get WHO identities; (2) seat cost per partner member; (3) base permission for members set to “No permission”; (4) members cannot create repositories or change visibility. Default: WHO GitHub owner and WHO IT to confirm | . | BD-03b | SHALL | A test account with partner-level access for the pilot. Default: WHO GitHub owner to provide one test account, removed after the build | . | BD-04 | SHALL | Repository roles. Default: Partners: Read on aai-programme; Maintain for the workstream lead and Write for the team on their own workstream repository; Triage on other workstream repositories where they contribute. Gates Foundation contacts: Read on aai-programme and the workstream repositories, and read access to the programme project | . | BD-05 | SHALL | Organisation owners willing to create issue fields and issue types. Default: One named WHO owner to run step 2 of section 13 | . | BD-05a | SHALL | Inspect the organisation’s existing issue fields before creating any new ones. Default: Reuse compatible existing fields; do not duplicate them | . | BD-06 | SHALL | Issue fields available on WHO’s GitHub plan and permitted by WHO enterprise policy. Default: Check and confirm | . | BD-07 | SHALL | Gates Foundation contacts have access to the programme project. Default: Decided: yes. They see everything that is shared, including delivery health and review status | . | BD-08 | SHALL | Credentials for the GitHub Actions in section 11. Workstream teams create these themselves. | . | DEP-02 | SHALL | A dependency becomes a D-number issue in aai-programme if it is programme-significant: it crosses workstreams or partners and needs a deadline, negotiation, escalation or an assessment of consequences. | . | DEP-03 | SHALL | Each D-number issue links to the waiting epic and to what it waits on. Where that is another epic and the relationship is a true blocking dependency, the agent also creates a native “blocked by” relationship between the two epics. Where the dependency is on a review, an external decision or a shared platform item, no native relationship is created. | . | DEP-04 | SHALL | The agent imports the existing dependency register (D01 to D29) as D-number issues in aai-programme. | . | DEP-05 | SHALL NOT | Do not create extra fields for waiting epic, epic waited on or needed-by date. d014a08f8674.title: Design principles
d014a08f8674.content: The principles every part of the build follows (section 2). Generated from requirements v0.5 by scripts/gen-requirements.ts; do not edit by hand. Cite one as req:aai-design-principles#<ID>. | ID | Level | Requirement | . | DP-01 | SHALL | Create once, show many times. One issue can appear in several projects. Never clone an issue to report its status somewhere else. | . | DP-02 | SHALL | Workstream leads own their delivery. The agent creates programme epics and the workstream template. It does not create features or stories in workstream repositories. | . | DP-03 | SHALL | Programme work is not sprint work. Sprints are managed inside the workstream projects. The programme project tracks dates, milestones, delivery health and readiness, not sprints. | . | DP-04 | SHALL | Open by default, and public. Everything on GitHub is public. What must not be public (section 6) is not put on GitHub. | . | DP-05 | SHALL | Technical integration judgements sit with the Technical Integration Lead. The Technical Integration Lead owns technical integration readiness and validation, working with the relevant workstream leads and subject-matter experts. The role is currently held by the WHO WS1 lead, but the authority comes from the role, not from WS1. The PM manages sequencing, dates, dependencies, evidence and escalation, and does not make technical readiness judgements. | . | DP-06 | SHALL | Automation must not make judgements. Automation may make deterministic administrative updates, such as adding items, lifecycle status changes and flags raised from labels. It never makes readiness, approval, risk-acceptance or decision judgements. | . | DP-07 | SHALL | Keep it simple. Delivery health, risk category, impact and dates only. No probability or impact scoring model. | . | DP-08 | SHALL | Prove it small before building it big. A pilot build (section 12) must pass before any bulk import. | . | DP-09 | SHALL | Plain language. All titles, field options, view names and READMEs use plain, simple English. Use the role name “PM & Architecture Integration” exactly as written. | .

7658cf4dbe64.title: Information classification
7658cf4dbe64.content: What may be on GitHub, which is public, and what never is (section 6). Generated from requirements v0.5 by scripts/gen-requirements.ts; do not edit by hand. Cite one as req:aai-information#<ID>. | ID | Level | Requirement | . | SEC-01 | SHALL | Treat everything on GitHub as public: title, body, comments, labels, issue fields, relationships, commit messages and attachments. | . | SEC-02 | SHALL | When an item has a note that is kept off GitHub, the issue may say so in neutral words, for example “A note is held by the PM”, and nothing more: no title, summary or link that hints at its content. | . | SEC-03 | SHALL | Write on the assumption that every partner, the funder and the public will read it. State facts and the next action, not blame. For example, “Blocked: waiting for the HIV graph schema from WS1, due 20 Nov” rather than an opinion on why. | . | SEC-04 | SHALL | Every repository and project the build creates is public. Before anything is imported, the PM removes from it what section 6 keeps off GitHub. | . | SEC-05 | SHALL NOT | Never weaken repository or project permissions beyond what BD-04 sets, and never change organisation-wide security settings. | .

9daf7acbcda3.title: How it fits together
9daf7acbcda3.content: . | The issues hold the values. Each programme field (section 7.1) is a label on the issue: ws:WS1 Knowledge graph, status:In progress, health:Blocked, stage:KG Knowledge graph, readiness:Validated, review-type:SME sign-off, review:Submitted, risk:Dependency, impact:Medium. They write labels, never the project. | Project 110 shows the issues through label filters. A view that needs a board column, a roadmap or a date needs a real project field, which nobody can set automatically without a token, so it is set by hand. | Issue types are type: labels (type:epic, type:feature, …): the items live in litlfred/aai-programme, outside the WHO organisation, so WHO’s issue types and issue fields do not apply to them (BD-02). | .
